title: VERIFICATION OF ADVANCED NAVIGATION ANTENNA - EXPRO+
description: Advanced satellite navigation antennas increasingly incorporate anti-jamming, anti-spoofing and adaptive beamforming capabilities to meet the growing demands of Positioning, Navigation and Timing (PNT) applications. The verification of such antennas requires realistic Over-The-Air (OTA) test environments capable of reproducing complex signal scenarios with multiple simultaneous sources arriving from different directions. Existing test approaches are often limited in their ability to reproduce realistic operational environments, leading to lengthy test campaigns and reduced capability to assess the full radiated performance of advanced navigation antennas.State-of-the-art OTA test systems based on multiple transmitting elements have demonstrated the capability to emulate representative signal environments for navigation applications. Such systems enable controlled reproduction of satellite constellations, interference sources, multipath conditions and other operational scenarios in a laboratory environment. However, current solutions oftensuffer from limited flexibility, restricted angular coverage, significant infrastructure requirements or insufficient scalability to support future generations of advanced navigation antennas.A compact, scalable and flexible OTA radiated test system based on an arrangement of transmitting elements surrounding the Antenna Under Test (AUT) needs to be developed. The developed system shall provide the capability to emulate realistic navigation signal environments, enabling repeatable laboratory verification of advanced navigation antennas and associated signal processing techniques. The system is intended to support the development and validation of future PNT technologies and shall constitute a versatile test capability for advanced navigation antenna assessment.Equipment already available at ESTEC, such as a general waveform generator (e.g. PSG) and signal analyser (e.g. PXA), and necessary for this activity will be reused for test execution.The objectives of this activity are: Develop a scalable OTA architecture based on multiple transmitting elements arranged around the Antenna Under Test. Demonstrate the capability of the system to reproduce multiple simultaneous signal sources with controlled angular distribution. Validate the performance of the developed system through representative OTA test campaigns.

title: DETERMINISTIC ETHERNET SPACE TIME-SENSITIVE NETWORKING SOFT IP CORE - EXPRO+
description: Objective:To develop a technology independent soft IP (Intellectual Property) core that complies with the aerospace profile of TSN(Time Sensitive Networking).Description:TSN (Time-Sensitive Networking) and TTE (Time Triggered Ethernet) are the two technologies that allow to deliver determinism and quality of service on top of standard Ethernet networks. Since TTE can be considered  relatively closed technology (i.e. proprietary solution, patents pending on the technology), since a few years TSN is emerging as a potential successor of that technology. TSN is IEEE supported set of standards that implements wide range of quality of services (i.e. reliability, determinism, mixed criticality traffic, redundancy, time synchronization) on top of the standard Ethernet protocols. TSN benefits from Ethernet Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) tools/ecosystem, it is free of patents and is being introduced step-by step in industrial applications (automotive/industrial) and aerospace domain (IEEE P802.1DP - TSN for Aerospace Onboard Ethernet Communications). Although TSN is very successful in the automotive/industrial sector, in space applications TSNis still being considered as low TRL technology. Many current and future Exploration and Space Transportationmissions are considering Ethernet-based networks for the data-handling communication bus. Having thistechnology available for future ESA missions is seen as a key driver for future missions. The aim of this activity Is to develop an IP core that contains the core functionalities of Time-Sensitive Networking needed for space applications. Although the set of TSN standards is very wide, there are several on-going activities aiming attailoring of TSN for space applications. Having an TSN IP tailored to space applications could be considered asa key enabler of this technology in future ESA and national missions.The following technical aspects shall be considered:- Development of End-system IP Core. Switch IP core is out of scope of this activity- One or two Ethernet ports shall be supported.- Host integration: AXI4 lite for registers and IP configuration, and AXI4 stream for packet data- The IP shall support 10/100/1000Mbps speeds. 10Gbps is considered optional.- Compatible and configurable with various PHY interfaces (i.e. MII/GMII/RGMIII).- To be developed as technology independent VHDL.- To be implemented and validated in 2 FPGA/ASIC technologies (preferable NG-Ultra/Ultra300 andMicrochip Polarfire).This activity encompasses the following tasks:- TSN IP core requirements identification and development of the high-level architecture of the TSN soft IP core.- Prototype development and integration into a representative Field-Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) based network platform.- Verification and validation targeting high speed use cases- TSN soft IP core release and related documentation.Deliverables: Prototype, Report, SoftwareApplication/Need Date: Exploration and Space Transportation missions. Mission Classification: alpha, beta,gamma, delta

title: IMPLEMENTATION AND MANAGEMENT OF ESA BUSINESS INCUBATION CENTRE CYPRUS
description: The network of ESA Business Incubation Centers (ESA BICs) is the largest network of space incubators in Europe. The two main objectives of an ESA BICs are to:Support entrepreneurs with a space-based business idea;Create and grow clusters of space related start-ups across Europe. All the ESA BICs are managed by local incubators with experience in supporting start-ups. They have good connections with local industry, universities, research organisations, as well as relevant government agencies and investor communities. ESA BICs follow the ESA BIC Common Approach to business incubation. So far, the network of ESA BICs has supported more than 2000 start-ups. Cyprus recently completed the ESA-Cyprus Plan for European Cooperating State (PECS) programme and recognized that Spaceis not only an important domain of research and development, but one of the key pillars of modern economy. On the 17th of March 2026, Cyprus became an Associate Member of the European Space Agency (ESA). The seven-year agreement opens the way for Cyprus's participation in ESA's optional programmes. As such, the Cypriot delegation asked ESA to start the implementation of an ESA BIC in Cyprus, under the ACCESS optional programme, in order to promote and foster the creation of startups active in the Space sector.  The objective is to find and support 15 space-related incubatees over an active period of four years, with additional two years added to thecontract duration to support any incubatees until the end of the incubation program. Each selected incubatee shall be entitled to an incentive funding of at least 60kEUR.

title: PHASE A SPACE BASED RE-ENTRY MONITOR - EXPRO+
description: Objectives and TasksThe activity aims to reach a preliminary design for a dedicated mission that will measure from orbit the destructive re-entry of artificial space objects in the Earth's atmosphere by means of a dedicated set of sensors. Pre-cursor sensor level activities haveidentified AlO (aluminium oxide band and associate lithium markers) and SWIR (shortwave infrared) as the most promising and accessible wavelengths from orbit that most re-entry events of artificial will have in common. The study shall establish the system level accommodation of such a sensor suite on a large CubeSat or small satellite platform with capable AOCS suite for pointing and orbit control.As uncontrolled or controlled re-entry events can occur anywhere on the globe, it is envisaged the satelliteplatform shall be in a relatively high orbit to ensure the field of view of the sensors can point to the re-entry streaks generated(which can last for 100'sof km) and preferential observation geometries (such as re-entry event in the Earth shadow) can be reached on average for 1 out of the on average 3 re-entries daily within the forecasting period of a ground segment (roughly two days prior to the event). The mobility needs of the platform shall thus be an integral part of the phase A level tradeoffs.To prepare for the above-described mission, the proposed activity will assess the overall feasibility of the mission and specifically include: Mission and requirements definition: redefine in detail the purpose and mission objectives deriving consistently the satellite system, theorbital, and the groundsegment requirements. These shall be derived from the identified need on regularly observing re-entry events. Conceptual design: based on the mission definition and system requirements, a conceptual design of the satellite will be developed. This includes the basiclayout of the satellite, the platform mass and size, the orbit, the major components and subsystems considering as well launch vehicle, and groundsegment. Definition of the payload (e.g. hyperspectral cameras and SWIR imagers). Identify all critical items (< TRL 6) and derive technology development plans for each including definition of the VV approach. Preliminary cost and schedule: estimate of costs and schedules is developed based on the conceptual design, and the system requirementsto be below 25MEUR. Risk assessment: risks associated with the mission and satellite design will be identified, evaluated, andassessed. Feasibility analysis: the feasibility of the mission and satellite design is assessed, taking into account technical, cost, and schedule considerations. Analysis of the commercialisation opportunities related to the mission concept and the related technologies.

title: CAPACITY DEVELOPMENT FACILITY EOAFRICA+
description: EO AFRICA+ is a 36-month capacity development facility designed to strengthen sustainable African capabilities in Earth Observation(EO) science, applications and innovation. Building on the achievements and community established through the EO AFRICA RD Facility, the activity will support African researchers, educators, institutions and early-career professionals in independently adopting, developing and applying EO technologies to address priority challenges across the continent.The facility combines curriculum development and Training of Trainers with a broad programme of face-to-face and online training, webinars, validation and field activities, and innovation challenges. It will strengthen the integration of EO into African higher education through reusable multilingual training materials and Africa-led training kits, while promoting practical learning and institutional uptake. Training will be supported by an open-source Training Management System and dedicated EO computing environments.EO AFRICA+ will foster African-European scientific cooperation through competitive Tandem RD Projects addressing priority African research challenges. The projects will combine skills transfer with access to advanced EO data, computing and open-science tools, producing reusable methods, software, datasetsand scientific outputs.A dedicated platform, implemented using ESA APEx, will provide the technical environment for practical training, research and prototyping. EO AFRICA+ will further strengthen the African EO community through outreach, an Advisory Board and broader community engagement, while supporting the long-term sustainability, reuse and African ownership of the capacities, knowledge and resources developed.
